# Quick guide to APA 7 citations {#sec-citas}

Examples of references in **APA style, 7th edition**, with documents that appear in this book. For cases not covered here, see the [official APA Style guide](https://apastyle.apa.org/) and follow your lecturer's instructions.

## In-text citations

| Case | Parenthetical citation | Narrative citation |
|---|---|---|
| One author | (Bates, 1989) | Bates (1989) |
| Two authors | (Metzger & Flanagin, 2013) | Metzger and Flanagin (2013) |
| Three or more | (Sugimoto et al., 2017) | Sugimoto et al. (2017) |
| Organisation | (American Psychological Association, 2020) | American Psychological Association (2020) |
| Direct quotation | (Bates, 1989, p. 410) | Bates (1989, p. 410) |
| Several works | (Bates, 1989; Marchionini, 2006) | — |

Use "&" between two authors inside parentheses and "and" in narrative citations. Quotations of fewer than 40 words go in quotation marks; longer ones go in an indented block without quotation marks.

## References

**Journal article with a DOI**

Metzger, M. J., & Flanagin, A. J. (2013). Credibility and trust of information in online environments: The use of cognitive heuristics. *Journal of Pragmatics*, *59*, 210-220. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pragma.2013.07.012

**Article with an article number instead of pages**

Walters, W. H., & Wilder, E. I. (2023). Fabrication and errors in the bibliographic citations generated by ChatGPT. *Scientific Reports*, *13*, Article 14045. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-41032-5

**Book**

Cruz Gil, C. (2015). *Modelos de búsqueda y recuperación de la información*. Trea.

**Edited book, online**

Bobish, G., & Jacobson, T. (Eds.). (2014). *The information literacy user's guide: An open, online textbook*. Open SUNY Textbooks. https://milnepublishing.geneseo.edu/the-information-literacy-users-guide-an-open-online-textbook/

**Conference paper in proceedings**

Bender, E. M., Gebru, T., McMillan-Major, A., & Shmitchell, S. (2021). On the dangers of stochastic parrots: Can language models be too big? In *Proceedings of the 2021 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency* (pp. 610-623). ACM. https://doi.org/10.1145/3442188.3445922

**Law (Spain)**

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1996, de 12 de abril, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Propiedad Intelectual [Royal Legislative Decree 1/1996 approving the consolidated text of the Intellectual Property Act]. *Boletín Oficial del Estado*, 97, 22 April 1996. https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1996-8930

**EU legislation**

Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence. *Official Journal of the European Union*, L, 12 July 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj

**Web page**

Caulfield, M. (2019, June 19). *SIFT (The four moves)*. Hapgood. https://hapgood.us/2019/06/19/sift-the-four-moves/

**Generative AI tool** (when its output is incorporated into the work)

Company. (Year). *Name of the tool* (version) [Large language model]. URL

Include the prompt used in the text or in an appendix, because readers cannot retrieve the conversation.

## Rules most often forgotten

- The list is ordered **alphabetically** by the first author's surname; two works by the same author, by year.
- **Hanging indent** (the first line of each reference sticks out) and double spacing in formal work.
- The **article title** is in roman type and sentence case; the **journal** and **volume** are in italics; the issue is in parentheses, in roman type.
- Write the DOI as a full link: `https://doi.org/…`, without "DOI:" in front.
- Up to **20 authors** are all listed in the reference; in the in-text citation, use "et al." for three or more from the first citation.
- Every in-text citation has its reference in the list, and every reference in the list is cited in the text.
